description: Joël Robuchon remains Las Vegas's most formal gastronomic address, an Art Deco townhouse-style dining room inside MGM Grand built around grand French tasting menus, bread carts, dessert carts and polished choreography. Its Forbes, La Liste and Wine Spectator signals keep it at the top of the city's affluent dining set even before the new Southwest Michelin selection is announced.
highlights: Grand French tasting-menu theatre with exceptional service, deep wine and one of the most luxurious dining rooms on the Strip.
sources: Forbes Travel Guide; La Liste 2026 via Las Vegas Review-Journal; Wine Spectator; Official restaurant website; Condé Nast Traveler

description: Restaurant Guy Savoy is the city's other defining French haute-cuisine room, tucked into Caesars Palace with a calm entrance that avoids the casino-floor rush. It is Guy Savoy's only restaurant outside France and remains a benchmark booking for black-truffle soup, serious wine, polished service and quiet special-occasion luxury.
highlights: Modern French haute cuisine, destination tasting menus, a Cognac lounge and a rare sense of calm inside Caesars Palace.
sources: Forbes Travel Guide; La Liste 2026 via Las Vegas Review-Journal; Official restaurant website; Condé Nast Traveler; Las Vegas Review-Journal Top 100

description: é by José Andrés is the tiny culinary theatre hidden inside Jaleo, where a handful of guests sit at a counter for a Spanish avant-garde tasting menu. It is one of the hardest reservations on the Strip and feels more intimate, playful and experimental than most resort flagships.
highlights: Eight-seat Spanish avant-garde counter with choreographed tasting-menu service inside The Cosmopolitan.
sources: Eater Vegas; Forbes Travel Guide; Official restaurant website; Condé Nast Traveler; Las Vegas Review-Journal Top 100

description: Wing Lei gives Las Vegas one of its most polished Chinese fine-dining rooms, a gold-toned Wynn setting built for Peking duck, seafood, wine and formal service. The restaurant's longevity and luxury-hotel execution make it a natural alternative to the city's French tasting-menu icons.
highlights: Forbes Five-Star Chinese fine dining with imperial design, Peking duck service and a refined Wynn atmosphere.
sources: Forbes Travel Guide; La Liste 2026 via Las Vegas Review-Journal; Wynn official website; Condé Nast Traveler; Eater Vegas

description: L'Atelier de Joël Robuchon translates the Robuchon vocabulary into a more kinetic counter-and-open-kitchen format at MGM Grand. It keeps the technical French cooking and serious wine credentials but offers a livelier, more design-forward way to book a luxury dinner.
highlights: Robuchon counter dining with French tasting menus, open-kitchen theatre and a more contemporary mood than the grand flagship next door.
sources: Forbes Travel Guide; Official restaurant website; Eater Vegas; Condé Nast Traveler; Las Vegas Review-Journal Top 100

description: Le Cirque is in its final Bellagio season but remains one of the city's most important formal dining rooms until its announced August 23, 2026 last service. The jewel-box room, French menu and long service legacy make it a current Las Vegas landmark rather than a nostalgic add-on.
highlights: Bellagio French institution in its final season, known for elegant service, jewel-box design and classic luxury dining rituals.
sources: Forbes Travel Guide; La Liste 2026 via Las Vegas Review-Journal; Bellagio official website; KTNV closure reporting; Condé Nast Traveler

description: Stubborn Seed brought Jeremy Ford's Miami tasting-menu sensibility to Resorts World, giving Las Vegas a current chef-driven room with energy beyond the legacy resort canon. It balances luxury ingredients, sharp plating and Strip polish with a more contemporary, less ceremonial attitude.
highlights: Jeremy Ford tasting-menu restaurant at Resorts World with modern American cooking and a polished but energetic room.
sources: Eater Vegas; Condé Nast Traveler; Forbes Travel Guide; Official restaurant website; Las Vegas Review-Journal Top 100

description: Kame Omakase is one of Las Vegas's most serious sushi splurges, a Chinatown counter built around premium fish, luxury add-ons and a small-room relationship between chef and guest. For diners who would otherwise book a formal tasting menu on the Strip, it offers a quieter and more product-focused alternative.
highlights: Intimate omakase counter with premium sourcing, luxury supplements and one of the city's most serious sushi followings.
sources: Eater Vegas; Condé Nast Traveler; Official restaurant website; Las Vegas Review-Journal Top 100; World of Mouth

description: ITO gives Fontainebleau a jewel-box omakase counter with the atmosphere of a private club rather than a casino restaurant. The restaurant's New York pedigree, 12-seat format and precise seafood focus make it one of the Strip's most relevant new luxury Japanese bookings.
highlights: Twelve-seat omakase counter at Fontainebleau with New York pedigree, premium seafood and a highly controlled guest experience.
sources: Condé Nast Traveler; Fontainebleau official website; Official restaurant website; Eater Vegas; Las Vegas Review-Journal Top 100

description: WAKUDA is a dramatic Japanese destination inside The Venetian, pairing modern Japanese cooking with a glossy room built for Strip-scale dining. It works for affluent guests who want the polish and scene of a resort restaurant without abandoning sushi, robata and crafted cocktails.
highlights: Design-heavy Japanese restaurant with sushi, robata, cocktails and a high-gloss Venetian setting.
sources: Condé Nast Traveler; Eater Vegas; Forbes Travel Guide; Official restaurant website; The Venetian official website

description: Bazaar Meat by José Andrés remains one of the city's defining modern steakhouses, now in a new Palazzo home that keeps the theatricality central to the experience. The room is built for serious spending, cured meats, fire, tasting menus and a sense of occasion that goes beyond a conventional chophouse.
highlights: Theatrical José Andrés steakhouse with fire-driven cooking, tasting-menu options and a polished Palazzo setting.
sources: Condé Nast Traveler; Eater Vegas; Official restaurant website; The Venetian official website; Forbes Travel Guide
hotel_name_hint: The Palazzo at The Venetian Resort

description: Gymkhana Las Vegas brings the London original's clubby Indian fine-dining idea to ARIA with a menu built around tandoor, game, curries and polished cocktails. Its arrival gives the Strip a rare Indian luxury restaurant that can genuinely compete for a special-occasion dinner slot.
highlights: Clubby Indian fine dining at ARIA from the acclaimed London restaurant group, with tandoor, curries, cocktails and a serious dinner format.
sources: Condé Nast Traveler; Eater Vegas; Official restaurant website; ARIA official website; Las Vegas Review-Journal

description: Carbone Riviera is the new Bellagio seafood and Italian-luxury successor in one of the city's most storied restaurant spaces. It channels Major Food Group glamour into seafood, tableside service and a lake-facing resort setting that is immediately relevant to high-spend Strip dining.
highlights: Major Food Group seafood-and-Italian luxury dining in the former Picasso space at Bellagio, with grand resort energy and prime views.
sources: Official restaurant website; Bellagio official website; Eater Vegas; Condé Nast Traveler; Las Vegas Review-Journal

description: Mizumi remains Wynn's most atmospheric Japanese dinner address, combining precise sushi and modern Japanese cooking with a garden, koi pond and waterfall setting. The restaurant's service, setting and product quality make it a classic luxury-resort alternative to a Western tasting menu.
highlights: Wynn Japanese dining with sushi, robatayaki, garden views, a koi pond and one of the Strip's most transporting resort settings.
sources: Forbes Travel Guide; Wynn official website; Condé Nast Traveler; Eater Vegas; Las Vegas Review-Journal Top 100

description: Michael Mina is a long-running Bellagio fine-dining anchor for refined seafood, caviar service, composed tasting menus and mature resort hospitality. It suits the guest who wants a polished, quieter alternative to the city's louder steakhouse and scene-restaurant circuits.
highlights: Refined Bellagio seafood dining with caviar, composed menus, deep wine and polished five-star resort service.
sources: Forbes Travel Guide; Official restaurant website; Eater Vegas; Condé Nast Traveler; Las Vegas Review-Journal Top 100

description: Partage is a polished French tasting-menu restaurant on Spring Mountain Road, proving that serious Las Vegas dining is not confined to the Strip. Its seasonal menus, chef focus and relatively intimate room make it a strong off-Strip choice for diners who care more about cooking than spectacle.
highlights: Off-Strip French tasting menus, refined plating and a serious wine-minded dinner experience in Chinatown.
sources: Eater Vegas; Official restaurant website; Las Vegas Review-Journal Top 100; World of Mouth; Condé Nast Traveler

description: Kaiseki Yuzu is one of the city's most disciplined Japanese dining rooms, focused on multi-course kaiseki rather than Strip glamour. The small scale, seasonality and craftsmanship make it a destination for guests who want a more culturally specific luxury dinner off the casino floor.
highlights: Serious kaiseki menus on Spring Mountain Road with a calm room, seasonal pacing and strong appeal for Japanese-food obsessives.
sources: Eater Vegas; Official restaurant website; Las Vegas Review-Journal Top 100; Condé Nast Traveler; World of Mouth

description: Kabuto Edomae Sushi is a compact Spring Mountain counter with a loyal following among serious sushi diners and chefs. Its appeal is quiet and product-led: rice, fish, knife work and pacing rather than resort drama.
highlights: Small Edomae sushi counter with omakase structure, chef-led pacing and a reputation that reaches far beyond its strip-mall setting.
sources: Eater Vegas; Condé Nast Traveler; 50 Best Discovery; Official restaurant website; Las Vegas Review-Journal Top 100

description: Vetri Cucina brings Marc Vetri's Italian fine-dining reputation to the top of the Palms, pairing handmade pasta with one of the city's most dramatic skyline views. The restaurant feels quieter than the central Strip but still works as a high-end, destination-level dinner.
highlights: Elevated Italian cooking and handmade pasta in a top-floor Palms room with sweeping Las Vegas views.
sources: Forbes Travel Guide; Official restaurant website; Eater Vegas; Condé Nast Traveler; Las Vegas Review-Journal Top 100

description: SW Steakhouse is Wynn's archetypal luxury steakhouse, pairing prime beef and seafood with Lake of Dreams views and one of the Strip's most reliable affluent dining rooms. It is a classic concierge recommendation because the setting, service and ingredient quality all match the price point.
highlights: Wynn steakhouse with prime beef, seafood, polished service and theatrical Lake of Dreams terrace appeal.
sources: Forbes Travel Guide; Wynn official website; Eater Vegas; Condé Nast Traveler; Las Vegas Review-Journal Top 100

description: CUT by Wolfgang Puck remains one of Las Vegas's most design-literate steakhouse rooms, with a polished Park MGM setting and a menu built around elite beef, seafood and martini-ready service. It is a serious business or special-occasion dinner that still feels contemporary.
highlights: Wolfgang Puck steakhouse with refined beef sourcing, polished service and a clean, modern resort dining room.
sources: Forbes Travel Guide; Official restaurant website; Eater Vegas; Condé Nast Traveler; Las Vegas Review-Journal Top 100

description: Bavette's gives Park MGM a darker, clubbier steakhouse that feels more like a grown-up supper room than a casino spectacle. The prime beef, seafood towers, cocktails and moody design make it one of the Strip's strongest instead-of-Michelin social dinners.
highlights: Moody Park MGM steakhouse with prime beef, seafood towers, strong cocktails and a clubby Chicago-meets-Vegas atmosphere.
sources: Condé Nast Traveler; Eater Vegas; Official restaurant website; Las Vegas Review-Journal Top 100; Forbes Travel Guide

description: Estiatorio Milos is a high-end Greek seafood institution on the Strip, built around pristine fish, raw bar displays, grilled seafood and a bright, urbane room. It is especially relevant for affluent diners who want seafood, freshness and scale without the formality of a tasting menu.
highlights: Luxury Greek seafood with whole fish, raw bar, grilled Mediterranean dishes and a sleek Venetian resort room.
sources: Forbes Travel Guide; Official restaurant website; Eater Vegas; Condé Nast Traveler; The Venetian official website

description: COTE Vegas imports the Korean steakhouse format into The Venetian with the polish expected from a luxury resort opening. The draw is premium beef cooked at the table, Korean accompaniments, a strong beverage program and enough glamour to function as a serious night out rather than a novelty concept.
highlights: Korean steakhouse at The Venetian with tableside grilling, premium beef, cocktails and a high-design resort setting.
sources: Condé Nast Traveler; Eater Vegas; Official restaurant website; The Venetian official website; Las Vegas Review-Journal

description: Mott 32 is one of the Strip's strongest upscale Chinese alternatives to Wing Lei, with a glamorous room, cocktails, dim sum, barbecue and signature apple-wood roasted Peking duck. It suits a social dinner where design, service and culinary credibility need to arrive together.
highlights: High-design Chinese dining with dim sum, barbecue, Peking duck, cocktails and a polished Venetian resort crowd.
sources: Condé Nast Traveler; Eater Vegas; Official restaurant website; Forbes Travel Guide; The Venetian official website

description: Delilah is the Wynn supper-club room that best captures Las Vegas's grown-up glamour, with a bandstand, plush banquettes, cocktails and refined American comfort cooking. It earns its place because the dinner, service and atmosphere work together, not merely because the room is famous.
highlights: Wynn supper club with live music, plush Art Deco glamour, cocktails and polished American dinner service.
sources: Condé Nast Traveler; Eater Vegas; Wynn official website; Forbes Travel Guide; Las Vegas Review-Journal Top 100

description: Casa Playa at Encore has become one of the most important modern Mexican rooms in Las Vegas, helped by Sarah Thompson's 2026 James Beard Best Chef: Southwest win. The restaurant combines coastal Mexican cooking, agave-focused drinks and a glamorous resort setting that feels genuinely dinner-led.
highlights: James Beard-recognized coastal Mexican cooking with grilled seafood, agave drinks and a high-energy Wynn/Encore room.
sources: James Beard Foundation; Eater Vegas; Wynn official website; Condé Nast Traveler; Las Vegas Review-Journal Top 100

description: Don's Prime gives Fontainebleau a classic new-money steakhouse with deep burgundy tones, tableside polish and a menu built around prime beef, seafood and martinis. It is a resort steakhouse for guests who want a more formal, polished room than the city's louder party concepts.
highlights: Fontainebleau steakhouse with prime beef, seafood, rich design and a grown-up luxury-resort mood.
sources: Eater Vegas; Condé Nast Traveler; Fontainebleau official website; Las Vegas Review-Journal Top 100; Forbes Travel Guide

description: Mother Wolf brings Evan Funke's Roman cooking to Fontainebleau with handmade pastas, wood-fired dishes and a grand, fashion-conscious room. It is less formal than the French icons but highly relevant for affluent diners who want a stylish Italian dinner with real culinary identity.
highlights: Roman-inspired Italian dining at Fontainebleau with handmade pasta, wood-fired cooking and a glamorous Strip room.
sources: Condé Nast Traveler; Eater Vegas; Fontainebleau official website; Las Vegas Review-Journal Top 100; Forbes Travel Guide

description: Sparrow + Wolf remains one of Chinatown's most credible chef-driven dinner rooms, combining global flavors, whole-animal sensibility, cocktails and a loyal local following. It gives affluent visitors a serious off-Strip option that still feels social, adult and distinctly Las Vegas.
highlights: Chef-driven Chinatown restaurant with global small plates, cocktails, wood-fire elements and a strong local following.
sources: Eater Vegas; Condé Nast Traveler; Official restaurant website; Las Vegas Review-Journal Top 100; World of Mouth

description: Golden Steer is the essential Old Vegas steakhouse, a red-leather, tableside-Caesar, celebrity-booth institution that still functions as a proper adult dinner. It is included as a protected informal local favorite because its cultural weight and enduring service rituals make it more than a retro novelty.
highlights: Old Vegas steakhouse institution with red leather booths, tableside Caesar, prime rib, martinis and deep local nostalgia.
sources: Eater Vegas; Condé Nast Traveler; Official restaurant website; Las Vegas Review-Journal Top 100; Travel + Leisure

description: Lotus of Siam is one of Las Vegas's defining local restaurants, famous for Northern Thai cooking, deep wine pairings and a national reputation earned long before the city became a celebrity-chef capital. The reopened East Sahara original gives the list a culturally essential relaxed dinner that sophisticated visitors still seek out.
highlights: Beloved Northern Thai institution with serious wine, local history and a reopened original East Sahara home.
sources: Eater Vegas; Condé Nast Traveler; Official restaurant website; Las Vegas Review-Journal Top 100; James Beard Foundation context

description: Raku is the chef-loved robata and izakaya restaurant that helped define Spring Mountain Road as an essential dining corridor. It is informal in format but serious in execution, with charcoal-grilled skewers, tofu, small plates and a late-night sophistication that still appeals to luxury diners.
highlights: Chef-loved robata and izakaya institution with charcoal grilling, small plates and an off-Strip local-dining identity.
sources: Condé Nast Traveler; Eater Vegas; Official restaurant website; Las Vegas Review-Journal Top 100; World of Mouth

description: Esther's Kitchen is the Arts District restaurant that made handmade pasta, sourdough and generous Italian-influenced cooking feel central to modern local Las Vegas dining. It is relaxed rather than luxurious, but its local importance, dinner energy and culinary consistency make it a natural informal favorite for well-traveled guests.
highlights: Arts District favorite for handmade pasta, sourdough, seasonal plates and a confident local dinner crowd.
sources: Eater Vegas; Condé Nast Traveler; Official restaurant website; Las Vegas Review-Journal Top 100; Resy

description: Bob Taylor's Ranch House is a mesquite-grill time capsule in northwest Las Vegas and a 2026 James Beard America's Classics honoree. Its distance from the Strip is justified by its age, local affection and Western dining identity, making it a meaningful relaxed dinner rather than a filler steakhouse.
highlights: Historic mesquite-grill ranch steakhouse, opened in 1955 and recognized by the James Beard Foundation as a 2026 America's Classics winner.
sources: James Beard Foundation; Eater Vegas; Official restaurant website; Las Vegas Review-Journal; local restaurant history sources
